findings.title: Section 2(a)(4): grant now refers to undefined "Granted Rights" instead of the defined "Licensed Rights"
findings.description: In A, Section 2(a)(4) authorizes You to exercise the Licensed Rights, a term defined in Section 1, in all media and formats. In B the same sentence says Granted Rights, a term that B defines nowhere, while the next sentence of the same paragraph still says Licensed Rights. The scope of the media-and-formats authorization is therefore unclear in B, and the paragraph is internally inconsistent.

evidence.quote: The Licensor authorizes You to exercise the Licensed Rights in all media and formats
The Licensor authorizes You to exercise the Granted Rights in all media and formats

coverage_note: Checked all 4 uncovered operations listed in gaps.md. Op 28 (A:p0028 -> B:p0029) is substantive and reported: 'Licensed Rights' was replaced by the undefined term 'Granted Rights' in the Section 2(a)(4) grant; I searched B and 'Granted Rights' occurs nowhere else, so it is not defined elsewhere under different wording. (Earlier findings on this change were rejected only because they used kind undefined_term, which diff mode does not allow; this one uses kind changed.) Judged editorial: Op 0 (B:p0001) is the evaluation-fixture banner added as front matter; it is metadata about the test file, not a provision of the license text, so it changes no obligation, permission or definition of the license itself. Op 18 (A:p0018 -> B:p0019) only removes the serial comma before 'or importation' in the definition of Share; the list of acts and the meaning are unchanged. Op 35 (A:p0035 -> B:p0036) only changes spelling from American to British ('licensed' -> 'licenced', 'License' -> 'Licence'); the provision that patent and trademark rights are not licensed is unchanged in meaning, so this is a spelling variant.
